minor.issue: Router at /app/backend/app/routers/quote_structure.py:44 accepts `payload: dict` and manually constructs `QuoteEnvironment(kind=payload.get('kind','other'), ...)`. If a client sends an invalid literal (e.g. 'living' instead of 'living_room'), pydantic ValidationError escapes the handler → 500 Internal Server Error instead of 422/400. Repro: POST body {name:'x', kind:'living'} → HTTP 500. FIX: swap payload:dict for a Pydantic Create-model (e.g. QuoteEnvironmentCreate) so FastAPI returns 422 automatically, OR wrap the model instantiation in try/except pydantic.ValidationError → HTTPException(422, ...). Same pattern likely exists in other routers that manually instantiate models from dict payloads — recommend audit.

`TenantEntitlementUpdate` (models_saas.py:113) does NOT expose `plan_snapshot_module_codes` as an updatable field, so any client attempt to modify the module list via PATCH is silently ignored (pydantic exclude_unset drops it, no error). Not a security bug (module dep enforcement happens on activation via set-module-state), but confusing DX: caller may believe the plan was patched. Consider either adding `plan_snapshot_module_codes: Optional[List[str]]` explicitly, or rejecting unknown fields with model_config extra='forbid'.
